source.title: Supernomial Coefficients, Bailey's Lemma and Rogers-Ramanujan-Type Identities. A Survey of Results and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Let (q)_m = product_{i=1}^m (1 - q^i), (q)_infinity = product_{i=1}^infinity (1 - q^i), and let [a choose b]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. For the A2 Rogers-Ramanujan identity (q)_infinity sum_{r1,r2>=0} q^(r1^2 - r1 r2 + r2^2)/((q)_{r1}(q)_{r2}(q)_{r1+r2}) = sum_{r1,r2>=0} q^(r1^2 - r1 r2 + r2^2)/(q)_{r1} [2r1 choose r2]_q = product_{n>=0} 1/((1 - q^(7n+1))^2 (1 - q^(7n+3)) (1 - q^(7n+4)) (1 - q^(7n+6))^2), find a partition-theoretic interpretation for the middle sum. Preferably, first rewrite the left-hand side as a q-series that is both manifestly of A2 type and manifestly coefficientwise positive, and then give a combinatorial interpretation of that positive series.

evidence.quote: It seems a worthwhile exercise to find a partition theoretic interpretation for the middle term
manifestly of A2-type as well as manifestly positive

accepted.question_text: Let C be the A2 Cartan matrix [[2,-1],[-1,2]]. For L=(L1,L2) in Z_+^2 and k=(k1,k2,k3) in Z^3 with k1+k2+k3=0, let S(L,k) be the normalized A2 supernomial S(L,k)=1/(q)_{CL} times the completely antisymmetric supernomial with top vector CL and lower vector L2(1,1,1)-k; the underlying supernomial is the finite Young-diagram-chain sum whose factors are Gaussian q-binomial coefficients. Restrict k to the dominant chamber k1>=k2>=k3 and set K=(k1+k2,k1). Since S(L,K) is nonzero exactly in the range K1<=L1, K2<=L2, 2K1>=K2, 2K2>=K1, 2L1>=L2, and 2L2>=L1, find an explicit closed formula for the inverse matrix Sbar(K,L) satisfying sum_{L1,L2>=0} Sbar(k,L) S(L,k') = delta_{k,k'} and sum_{dominant k, |k|=0} S(L,k) Sbar(k,L') = delta_{L,L'}. Partial formulas are known for K=(r,2r-p) with p=0,1,2,3; the goal is a formula for arbitrary K.

evidence.quote: The A2 analogue of the inversion formula
we failed to observe enough regularity to guess

accepted.question_text: Develop an arbitrary-rank A_{n-1} version of the Bailey-type summations that include the A1 q-binomial invariance sum and the two A2 supernomial summations used to iterate identities. In this setting S(L,k) denotes the normalized A_{n-1} supernomial with L in Z_+^{n-1}, k in Z^n, and |k|=0. The desired arbitrary-rank theorem should be strong enough to iterate identities, not merely the known weak form sum_{L in Z_+^{n-1}} q^(L C L/2) S(L,k) = q^((k1^2+...+kn^2)/2)/(q)_infinity^{n-1}, because that weak form produces a new q-series identity but cannot be iterated indefinitely.

Prove the proposed level-N A_{n-1} string-function generalization of the weak Bailey summation. More explicitly, for n>=2, N>=1, k in Z^n with |k|=0, normalized A_{n-1} supernomials S(L,k), and the level-N A_{n-1} string function C_k(q) represented by a sum over eta in Z^{n-1} tensor Z^{N-1}, show that the double sum over L in Z_+^{n-1} and eta with exponent (L C L)/(2N) + eta(C tensor C^{-1})eta/2 and q-binomial factor [(mu+eta) choose eta]_q equals q^((k1^2+...+kn^2)/(2N)) C_k(q). The variables eta and mu must obey the source's integrality constraints, including that mu is fixed by (C tensor I)eta + (I tensor C)mu = C L tensor e_{N-1}. The case n=2 is known; the open goal is the general case.

evidence.quote: natural to ask for a generalization
A proof of conjecture 6.3 for n = 2

accepted.question_text: For the A3 case, find a sufficiently simple closed expression for the more general summation sum_{L in Z_+^3} q^(L C L/2) S(L,k)/(q)_{M-L}, where M is an arbitrary element of Z_+^3, C is the A3 Cartan matrix, and S(L,k) is the normalized A3 supernomial. The expression should be simple enough, after any necessary extraction of common factors, to indicate how the A3 Bailey-type summation can be iterated beyond the isolated single-parameter A3 result sum_{L in Z_+^3} q^(L C L/2) S(L,k)/(q)_{M2-L2}.

evidence.quote: we have not found a sufficiently simple expression
to suggest how (after taking out possible factors) to iterate further

accepted.question_text: Prove the A_{n-1} supernomial hierarchy identity conjectured for n>=2 and p>=n. Define F_{p,L}(q) by the tensor-product sum over mu subject to the integrality condition (C^{-1} tensor I)mu integral, with eta=L tensor e_1 - (C^{-1} tensor C)mu. For L in Z_+^{n-1}, k in Z^n with |k|=0, rho=(1,2,...,n), and S_n the symmetric group, prove that sum_{|k|=0} sum_{sigma in S_n} epsilon(sigma) q^(1/2 sum_i (p k_i - 2 sigma_i) k_i) S(L, p k - sigma + rho) = F_{p,L}(q), where S is the normalized A_{n-1} supernomial. The cases p=n and p=n+1 are already established, so the open content is the remaining cases.

evidence.quote: an infinite hierarchy of A2 supernomial identities was conjectured
for p = n + 1 a proof has been found

accepted.question_text: Prove the cylindric-partition-motivated identity involving the product T''(L,M,k,k') = product_{i=1}^n [M+L-k_i+k'_i choose L-k_i]_q for L,M in Z_+ and zero-sum integer vectors k,k'. For p>=n, show that the signed A_{n-1} sum over |k|=0 and sigma in S_n of q^{phi_{p,k,sigma}} T''(L,M, p k - sigma + rho, (p-1)k - sigma + rho) equals the corresponding mu-sum with exponent mu(C^{-1} tensor C)mu/2, the q-binomial factor [M+nL - sum_b C^{-1}_{1,b} mu^{(b)}_1 choose nL]_q, and the factor [mu+eta choose mu]_q, where eta=nL(C^{-1}e_1 tensor e_1) - (C^{-1} tensor C)mu and the mu-sum uses the same integrality restriction as the supernomial hierarchy. The case p=n+1 is known from the cited Gessel-Krattenthaler identity; the open problem is the general conjecture supported by computer checks.

evidence.quote: For p = n + 1 the above is identity

accepted.question_text: Find a closed-form generalized supernomial T(L,M,k,k') for n>=3 that realizes the unifying A_{n-1} identity suggested by the three conjectures in Section 7. The function should satisfy the limiting conditions that recover T((M1,M2),k)(q)_{M1+M2}, the reciprocal supernomial T'(L,k), and the cylindric-partition product T''(L1,M1,k,k'), and it should obey the reciprocal-q constraint T(L,M,k,k';1/q)/T(L,M,k,k';q)=q^(-M C L + sum_i k_i k'_i). The goal is an explicit closed form for T that makes the unifying signed sum identity valid when n>=3.

evidence.quote: strongly suggest the existence of a unifying identity
we have not succeeded in finding a closed form expression when n >= 3

evidence.quote: How to make this manifest is unclear to us.
